_note: Age cohorts, consumption, and the birth lottery that caps growth to what the settlement can sustain. Cohorts consume regardless of whether they work, which is what makes the dependency ratio a real constraint and the lottery a genuinely political instrument.

cohorts.name: Apprentices
cohorts._note: Eat more than adults and work less. Putting them to work early is an option with a morale and legitimacy cost.

cohorts.name: Elders
cohorts._note: The Advisory Board is drawn from here. A Shaft that treats its elders badly is arguing with its own government.

birthLottery._note: Caps growth to sustainable levels. Reaction depends on perceived FAIRNESS, not on the number of slots — a lottery seen as rigged costs more trust than a stingy one seen as honest.

health._note: Air quality is the biggest single health driver, which is what connects the per-level air model to the population model rather than leaving it a standalone gauge.
